NEW DELHI: The Supreme Court on Friday ordered that the traditional Karthigai Deepam lamp will be lit again on Saturday atop the Deepathoon. It also suspended the Tamil Nadu temple's board of trustees, appointed two retired Madras High Court judges as receivers to manage the temple, and handed over security of the temple and Thiruparankundram hill to the CRPF This order came days after Karthigai Deepam lamp was lit at the Deepa Mandapam near the Ucchi Pillayar temple, instead of Deepathoon as ordered earlier by the Supreme Court.A bench of Justices Aravind Kumar and Vipul M Pancholi said it would take action against anyone attempting to create constitutional chaos.Solicitor General Tushar Mehta, appearing for the Archaeological Survey of India (ASI), told the bench that temple trustees had informed the agency that they had received no instructions from higher officials regarding the entry.Also read: 'Time to deal with iron hand' - SC comes down heavily on Vijay government over Deepam row Here's what SC ordered:The Supreme Court directed that the traditional Karthigai Deepam lamp be lit atop the disputed Deepathoon pillar on Saturday, using the flame lit at the Uchaipillaiyar mandapam. The court had earlier permitted the ritual as a one-time interim measure on November 24, but the lamp was lit only at the customary mandapam and not at Deepathoon.The Supreme Court suspended the board of trustees of the Arulmigu Subramaniaswamy temple and appointed two retired Madras High Court judges, Justice S Vaidyanathan and Justice V Parthipan, as receivers to take over its management.It also handed over security of the temple and Thiruparankundram hill to the CRPF.The bench issued contempt notices to Tamil Nadu Chief Secretary, Director General of Police (DGP), Madurai Collector and other officials over the alleged violation of its November 20 order permitting the lighting of the Karthigai Deepam lamp at Deepathoon. Observing that the state executive authorities appeared to have acted on the "diktats of their political bosses", the court directed the chief secretary to appear personally and file an affidavit detailing the emails, phone calls and messages exchanged between officials in connection with the matter.The bench said, "The wilful non-compliance of orders of the Court, especially by the executive authorities, cannot go unnoticed and it has to be dealt with an iron hand." It also observed that the conduct of the officials prima facie indicated administrative chaos in the state. Describing the alleged actions as "a brazen and wilful disobedience" of its order and "a calculated affront to the authority of both constitutional courts", the court warned that attempts to undermine the course of justice would not be tolerated.It further clarified that its orders were binding on the state, its officials and every religious institution, and were not an invitation to negotiate.Expressing "pain and anguish" over the failure to implement its earlier order, the bench said, "The time has come to deal with the situation with an iron hand as it will lead to constitutional chaos."It also warned that it would "set right anybody trying to create constitutional chaos", making it clear that its directions could not be diluted.
Article Summary: The traditional Karthigai Deepam lamp will be lit again on Saturday atop the Deepathoon. It also suspended the Tamil Nadu temple's board of trustees, appointed two retired Madras High Court judges as receivers to manage the temple. The bench issued contempt notices to Tamil Nadu Chief Secretary, Director General of Police, Madurai Collector and other officials.

Article Title: ‘Today one Deepam, tomorrow temples?’ Vaishnaw slams TVK govt over Thiruparankundram Deepam row
Article Text:
Vaishnaw slams TVK government over Thiruparankundram Deepam row in Tamil Nadu

NEW DELHI: Railway minister Ashwini Vaishnaw on Thursday launched a sharp attack on the Tamil Nadu government over the Thiruparankundram Karthigai Deepam row, accusing it of hurting the religious sentiments of millions. He also cautioned the state government against attempts to restrict temple traditions and religious practices.Addressing a Constitution Day event organised by the BJP in Chennai, Vaishnaw further targeted the Congress, accusing it of placing family interests above constitutional values.Referring to the dispute over lighting the ceremonial lamp at the Deepathoon stone pillar, Vaishnaw questioned the Vijay government's position and warned that restrictions on religious practices could have wider implications."Tamil Nadu is intact. Stopping one deepam, you have stopped, you have hurt, you have destroyed and disturbed the emotions of millions of people. What will happen? Today you have stopped one deepam, tomorrow you will say that nobody can go to a temple? They'll shut down the temples. Is that what they want?" he said, according to news agency PTI.Vaishnaw also said, "True respect for the Constitution means safeguarding religious freedom and taking pride in our culture, Lord Muruga, and our ancient heritage."The remarks came amid continuing tensions over the annual Karthigai Deepam ceremony. Maha Deepam was lit above the Uchi Pillayar temple at Thiruparankundram Hills amid heavy security, but no lamp was lit at the disputed Deepathoon pillar. A team of priests associated with the Subramaniaswamy temple performed the ceremony at the usual location.The dispute escalated after a scuffle broke out between members of Hindu organisations and police. Several people, including BJP leaders and members of Hindu outfits, were detained amid restrictions imposed by authorities over law-and-order concerns.The matter is also before the Supreme Court. On Thursday, a bench of Justices Aravind Kumar and Vipul M Pancholi said contempt petitions and other applications concerning the non-lighting of the lamp at Deepathoon would be listed on November 27."Everything will be listed tomorrow," the bench said. The Tamil Nadu government had apologised to the court on Wednesday over the incident, blaming the temple authorities. The apex court had earlier declined to initiate suo motu contempt proceedings.Vaishnaw also criticised the Congress over the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls and electronic voting machines (EVMs), alleging that the party questioned electoral processes selectively."Congress wants to just blame SIR for their own failures. And they will keep failing like this. Because for them, it is not the Constitution, it is the family," he said.Turning to railway development, the minister claimed that Tamil Nadu had acquired only 1,253 hectares, or 24 per cent, of the approximately 4,800 hectares required for railway projects.He urged the state government to expedite land acquisition, assuring that the Centre would provide the necessary funds. Vaishnaw also highlighted the redevelopment of 77 railway stations in Tamil Nadu and discussed proposed high-speed rail connectivity between Chennai, Bengaluru and Hyderabad.The Supreme Court's scheduled hearing on Saturday is expected to bring further clarity to the contempt petitions and applications.
Article Summary: Railway minister Ashwini Vaishnaw slams TVK government over Thiruparankundram Deepam row. Accuses Tamil Nadu government of hurting religious sentiments of millions. Warns against attempts to restrict temple traditions and religious practices. Further criticised Congress for placing family interests above constitutional values.

Article Title: 'Fake news': CJP's Ranka threatens legal action over claim leaders fled Nagpur rally venue after Look Out Circulars issued
Article Text:
CJP’s Ranka accuses news agency of ‘fake news’ over leaders’ rally exit amid LOC row

NEW DELHI: Cockroach Janta Party ( CJP ) co-convenor Ashutosh Ranka has threatened legal action against news agency IANS, accusing it of spreading fake news over a video posted on X. The agency had claimed that CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke and his associates left a venue after receiving information about a Look Out Circular (LOC), while avoiding media cameras.In its post, IANS wrote: "As soon as they received information about the Look Out Notice, CJP Founder Abhijeet Dipke and his associates began leaving the spot while avoiding media cameras. They left before Actor Prakash Raj could speak."Responding to the post, Ranka said the agency had published an inaccurate account of the events and warned it to expect a legal notice."Dear IANS, Instead of posting from the IT cell account, you accidentally posted from your official id. You might now wait for a legal notice for spreading fake news, since there are videos of Prakash Sir addressing the audience and all of us comfortably leaving the venue with police around," he wrote on X.The video posted by IANS showed reporters following vehicles carrying CJP leaders as they left the venue. It later showed actor Prakash Raj being escorted by a police official as media personnel gathered around him. However, the footage does not establish the context claimed in the agency's post.The exchange came amid a protest organised by the CJP in Nagpur on Thursday, where Dipke and other party leaders addressed a rally titled 'Save Democracy, Save Constitution' at Samvidhan Chowk on Constitution Day.Addressing the gathering, Dipke accused the BJP-led Centre of undermining the Constitution and alleged that institutions across the country had been hijacked."The government is acting against the Constitution. Not a single institution is left that has not been hijacked," he said.Referring to the LOC issued against him by Mumbai Police, Dipke challenged the authorities to arrest him."There is a lookout notice against me by the Mumbai Police. There is police bandobast here and they are looking for me. Where is Abhijeet Dipke? I am here in Samvidhan Chowk. What will you do? Arrest me. I have been in jail twice. Don't show me the fear of jail," he said.Ranka, meanwhile, said the party was preparing to expand its activities beyond protests in major cities. "We will go to every village, interact with people and give a voice to the youth," he said.Mumbai Police have issued LOCs against Dipke, Ranka and CJP leader Saurav Das in connection with an FIR over an alleged unauthorised protest at Shivaji Park on Gandhi Jayanti. Police said the circulars were issued to prevent the leaders from leaving the country while the investigation was underway.Das was stopped at the airport on November 23 while attempting to travel to the United Kingdom for an event at Oxford University. He has challenged the LOC before the Delhi High Court.
Article Summary: CJP co-convenor Ashutosh Ranka has threatened legal action against news agency IANS. Ranka accused IANS of spreading fake news over a video posted on X. The agency had claimed that CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke and his associates left a venue after receiving information about a Look Out Circular.

Article Title: 'Money-minded manifesto': Mayawati slams Akhilesh Yadav's SP ahead of 2027 UP polls
Article Text:
Mayawati slams Akhilesh Yadav

NEW DELHI: Bahujan Samaj Party (BSP) chief Mayawati on Friday launched a sharp attack on the Samajwadi Party (SP) over its recently released 'Manifesto of the People's Will' for the 2027 Uttar Pradesh Assembly elections, dismissing it as "little more than empty rhetoric" and a "money-minded manifesto" rather than a genuine commitment to public welfare.In a post on X, the former Uttar Pradesh chief minister said the SP's manifesto was similar to its 'PDA' (Pichhda, Dalit, Alpsankhyak) initiative and reflected the saying "all show, no substance".Mayawati alleged that the SP had consistently followed a "narrow-minded, casteist and pro-big business" approach that went against the interests, welfare, dignity and security of poor people, Dalits, backward classes, Muslims and other sections of society.She also cited the SP's alleged preference for a wealthy businessperson over supporting the PDA in the recent biennial Rajya Sabha elections from Uttar Pradesh as an example of its political approach.Questioning whether such policies could address the state's problems, including poverty, unemployment, backwardness and migration, Mayawati said the SP's manifesto was more concerned with financial interests than public welfare.She further alleged that the party would continue to field wealthy candidates and strongmen rather than people committed to public and social interests.Defending her party's record, Mayawati said the principles of "work for every hand" and "the rule of law through the law" belonged to the BSP and had been implemented during all four of its governments in Uttar Pradesh.She also accused the SP of having a record of opposing reservations for Scheduled Castes (SCs), Scheduled Tribes (STs) and Other Backward Classes (OBCs), and of contributing to caste-based hostility and riots in the state.In her post, she described the SP's promises and declarations as "electoral deception and trickery", urging voters to remain cautious.Mayawati pitches BSP as authentic Ambedkarite partyWith Assembly elections approaching in Uttar Pradesh, Uttarakhand and Punjab, Mayawati called for strengthening the BSP, describing it as the only authentic Ambedkarite party capable of translating the ideals of the Constitution into reality.“Given that the general assembly elections—particularly in Uttar Pradesh, as well as in Uttarakhand and Punjab—are fast approaching, it is imperative to effectively translate the noble intent of Babasaheb Dr. Bhimrao Ambedkar’s Constitution into reality. This cannot be achieved through the mindset or working culture of narrow-minded, feudal, or casteist parties; rather, it can only be realised through the advancement of the BSP—the sole, authentic Ambedkarite party—which guarantees the welfare of all sections of society and ensures the safety of their lives, property, and religious beliefs, while fostering the upliftment of the 'Bahujan Samaj’," she said.Mayawati said the BSP aimed to establish the rule of law in Uttar Pradesh and promote a governance model centred on public welfare, social well-being and development.“So that an 'iron rule of law' can be established here in UP, along with a governance model rooted in the principle of 'the welfare and happiness of all '—prioritising public interest, social well-being, and development. This would enable all sections of society—currently plagued by poverty, unemployment, backwardness, and the distress of forced migration—to lead a prosperous life filled with peace and happiness,” she added.The BSP, which governed Uttar Pradesh from 2007 to 2012, was reduced to a single seat in the 2022 Assembly elections despite securing more than 13 per cent of the vote share.The party failed to win a single seat in the 2024 Lok Sabha elections.SP-Congress seat-sharing talks continueMeanwhile, the SP is preparing to contest the 2027 Uttar Pradesh Assembly elections in alliance with the Congress. The two INDIA bloc partners are continuing negotiations over seat-sharing, with the SP having offered 26 seats to the Congress in the initial round of discussions.The Congress, however, has sought 120 seats and is unwilling to accept a lower number, according to sources.The SP is seeking to return to power after consecutive defeats in the 2017 and 2022 Assembly elections. It won 111 seats in the 2022 polls.
Article Summary: Bahujan Samaj Party (BSP) chief Mayawati slams Samajwadi Party (SP) over its recently released 'Manifesto of the People's Will' for the 2027 Uttar Pradesh Assembly elections. Former Uttar Pradesh chief minister said the SP's manifesto was similar to its 'PDA' (Pichhda, Dalit, Alpsankhyak) initiative.

NEW DELHI: Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav on Friday attacked the ruling BJP over the proposed delimitation-linked women's reservation bill, saying it would prove to be the party's “biggest political mistake”.“Delimitation will prove to be the biggest political mistake made by the BJP,” Akhilesh said in a post on X.His remarks came a day after the government announced a special sitting of Parliament from November 30 to December 3 to transact “essential” business, amid speculation that it may reintroduce the delimitation-linked women's reservation bill.The proposed legislation seeks to increase the Lok Sabha's strength from 543 to a maximum of 850 seats through delimitation, paving the way for the implementation of 33% reservation for women in Parliament and state legislatures ahead of the 2029 general elections.Congress also alleged that the special session had little to do with women's reservation and accused the government of using it to push the delimitation bill.“Yet again, the mischievous PM-HM jodi is lying,” Congress general secretary Jairam Ramesh said on X.Ramesh pointed out that the Nari Shakti Vandan Adhiniyam, providing one-third reservation for women, was passed unanimously by Parliament in September 2023.The Congress president had subsequently demanded its immediate implementation, but the law was not notified until 10.40 pm on April 16, 2026, he said.“The Special Session is thus NOT for women's reservation. That is already a law which the PM-HM jodi have put into cold storage for over three years,” Ramesh said.He alleged that the government was convening Parliament to push delimitation and redraw constituencies to benefit the BJP.“And who will be in charge of deciding the geography of constituencies? It will be a thoroughly compromised and brutally exposed CEC, Gyanesh Kumar, who has made a complete mockery of preparation of electoral rolls and destroyed the integrity of the electoral process,” he said.“The executors of Vote Chori on such a gigantic scale are to be given the powers to carry out delimitation and manipulate the nature of constituencies. This is as atrocious as you can get.“This is a desperate move by a nervous and rattled PM who is under siege. It will be countered with firm resolve,” Ramesh added.The Congress has also alleged that the government is hoping to secure a “super-tainted” two-thirds majority to pass the Constitution amendment bill.Shiv Sena (UBT) leader Sanjay Raut also opposed the proposed delimitation exercise, alleging that it was a BJP conspiracy to take away people's political power.Sharing a post on X, Raut said, “Today, Shiv Sena chief Balasaheb Thackeray is no longer with us: Sharad Pawar is unwell and in no position to fight or make decisions, otherwise the anti-national Delimitation Bill would never have dared to be brought before Parliament in such a corrupt manner: Delimitation is a BJP conspiracy to strip the people of this country of their power.”“Anyone who supports it is betraying the people of this country… They will be known as the biggest traitors of the 21st century! Therefore, every patriotic, democratic party should reject Delimitation in Parliament. History always remembers the names of traitors; Explanations for betrayal fade into thin air” he added.Meanwhile, the YSR Congress Party (YSRCP) is likely to support the delimitation bill, provided it ensures regional balance, party sources told ANI.The Lok Sabha Secretariat said the second part of the eighth session of the 18th Lok Sabha will begin on November 30. The special sitting is expected to conclude on December 3, subject to the exigencies of government business.The sittings will be an extension of the Monsoon Session, which was adjourned sine die on August 13 but not prorogued.Earlier on Thursday, Union parliamentary affairs minister Kiren Rijiju said the government had requested the Lok Sabha Speaker and Rajya Sabha Chairman to reconvene the Houses to transact essential government business.The Union Cabinet is also scheduled to meet on Friday and is likely to discuss the delimitation-linked women's reservation legislation, sources said.The developments follow Prime Minister Narendra Modi's remarks on Thursday, accusing an opposition party of blocking the Constitution (131st Amendment) Bill, 2026, in April.In a signed article published in newspapers, PM Modi, “The journey of our Constitution would be incomplete without recognising the remarkable women who helped shape it. But what happened earlier this year should fill our hearts with shame.”“I assure the 'Nari Shakti' of India that no force can prevent us from ensuring that justice is done to them,” he added.The bill was defeated in April after the government failed to secure the required two-thirds majority in the Lok Sabha. It needs 361 votes in the 543-member House, which currently has 540 members due to three vacancies.The NDA has around 320 MPs and would require additional support from opposition parties to cross the threshold.The government's position has strengthened since the bill's defeat in April, with 26 MPs moving out of the opposition camp.Twenty rebel Trinamool Congress MPs broke away and merged with the Nationalist Citizens Party of India (NCPI), pledging support to the NDA, while six Shiv Sena (UBT) MPs joined the Eknath Shinde-led Shiv Sena.However, the ruling alliance still needs additional votes. The DMK, with 22 Lok Sabha MPs, and the NCP (SP), with eight, could play a significant role in the evolving political arithmetic.Opposition parties are also expected to raise their protests against the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls and demand the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar, potentially leading to another stormy session.
Article Summary: The proposed legislation seeks to increase the Lok Sabha's strength from 543 to a maximum of 850 seats. It would pave the way for the implementation of 33% reservation for women in Parliament and state legislatures ahead of the 2029 general elections. The government announced a special sitting of Parliament from November 30 to December 3.

Article Title: 'Wish Akhilesh spent 6 months in jail': Azam Khan quips; gets witty reply from SP chief
Article Text:
Azam Khan said he wished party chief Akhilesh Yadav had spent at least six months in prison.

Azam Khan recalls 'prison trauma'

Khan's repeated stints behind bars

NEW DELHI: Samajwadi Party veteran Azam Khan on Thursday said he wished party chief Akhilesh Yadav had spent at least six months in prison to understand the emotional and physical hardships of incarceration.Akhilesh Yadav responded that he had felt Khan's pain over the years, adding a light-hearted remark about the jails built during the SP's tenure.The exchange took place at the launch of the SP's manifesto for the 2027 Uttar Pradesh Assembly elections. Khan also spoke about the distress of being separated from his son Abdullah during a prison transfer and the fear that they might never see each other again.Recalling his time behind bars, Khan said he would sometimes tell Abdullah and other inmates that he wished Yadav could experience prison life, even if only for six months."My heart wished Akhilesh ji, too, could come to jail for six months, so he could know how the days and nights pass and what one goes through," Khan said.Asked by reporters about Khan's remarks after the manifesto launch, Yadav said, "He is a member of our party and our family. I have felt his pain from time to time."Yadav also responded with a quip about the prisons constructed when the SP was in power."I told Azam Khan that SP built best jails in Etawah during its tenure.We will also work on how to further improve jails in future," he said.Khan described his separation from Abdullah during a transfer between prisons as one of the most painful experiences of his incarceration. He said the uncertainty over his son's whereabouts left him fearing that they might never meet again.The veteran leader also spoke about having to see his young son remain in prison with him for years. Earlier at the event, Yadav had assured Khan that the party would do whatever was necessary to fulfil the promises made in its manifesto.The 10-time MLA from Rampur served as a cabinet minister in the Akhilesh Yadav-led government between 2012 and 2017, holding portfolios including parliamentary affairs and urban development.He was released from Dasna jail in Ghaziabad on November 18 after the Allahabad high court granted him interim bail in a money laundering case registered by the Enforcement Directorate in connection with the Maulana Mohammad Ali Jauhar University in Rampur.The ED had arrested Khan on October 31, shortly after he was released from Rampur jail in another case. He had spent nearly 11 months behind bars during that earlier stint.Yadav has met Khan during some of his periods in custody. He visited him at Sitapur jail shortly after his arrest in February 2020 and again in March 2024, ahead of the Lok Sabha elections, to discuss candidate selection in Rampur and neighbouring constituencies.During Khan's latest incarceration, Yadav met him at Rampur jail on October 22, 2026, for around 45 minutes ahead of the 2027 Assembly elections.
Article Summary: Azam Khan said he wished party chief Akhilesh Yadav had spent at least six months in prison. Khan also spoke about the distress of being separated from his son Abdullah during a prison transfer. Yadav responded that he had felt Khan's pain over the years, adding a light-hearted remark about the jails built during the SP's tenure.

Article Title: Bihar move illegal, says Supreme Court, quashes premature release of former MP Anand Mohan
Article Text:
The state govt had amended prison rules to pave the way for Mohan’s release by removing the provision that disqualifies a person from remission if he is convicted of a public servant’s murder.

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Quoting former US President Theodore Roosevelt to say justice consisted not in being neutral between right and wrong, but in finding out the right and upholding it, the Supreme Court Thursday quashed Bihar’s decision to allow the premature release of former MP and strongman Anand Mohan in the 1994 lynching case of district magistrate G Krishnaiah.The state government had amended prison rules to pave the way for Mohan’s release by removing the provision that disqualifies a person from remission if he is convicted of a public servant’s murder. A bench of Justices Dipankar Datta and Sheel Nagu quashed the amendment, saying it was indefensible and no rationale was given for changing the law. It directed Mohan to surrender within a month.“The notification dated April 10, 2023, is declared unconstitutional, invalid and inoperative, and is hereby set aside. The order dated April 24, 2023, granting premature release to (Mohan), is hereby quashed,” the bench said.The court said the state government could initiate a fresh procedure to amend the remission policy. “It is clarified that any future process to revise or amend Rule 481 shall not be initiated prior to (Mohan) surrendering within a month or being taken into custody, as the case may be,” it said.
Article Summary: The Supreme Court Thursday quashed Bihar’s decision to allow the premature release of former MP and strongman Anand Mohan in the 1994 lynching case of district magistrate G Krishnaiah. The state government had amended prison rules to pave the way for Mohan's release. A bench of Justices Dipankar Datta and Sheel Nagu quashed the amendment.

NEW DELHI: The Gujarat ATS has foiled an alleged terror plot targeting the Indian Air Force (IAF) station in Vadodara, arresting a suspected Jaish-e-Mohammed operative who was allegedly preparing to launch an attack with an AK-47-style assault rifle, officials said on Friday.The accused, identified as Mohammad Islam Kabiruddin, a native of Assam, had arrived in Vadodara after switching off his regular mobile phone and was staying at a hotel, Gujarat ATS DIG Sunil Joshi said.The ATS had received intelligence that a person from another state, affiliated with JeM, was planning to enter Gujarat in the coming days with an automatic assault rifle to target a security establishment."ATS received information that an individual from another state, affiliated with Jaish-e-Mohammed, was planning to enter Gujarat within the coming days, armed with an automatic assault rifle, with the intent of attacking a security establishment," Joshi said.The search led to the recovery of an automatic assault rifle resembling an AK-47-style, two empty magazines, 23 live cartridges, a Jaish-e-Mohammed flag, mobile phones, SIM cards and cash from his bag, the DIG added.Kabiruddin's handler was identified as Mufti Rafiq, alias Ibn Abdullah, who is affiliated with Jaish-e-Mohammed, the ATS DIG said. The handler had allegedly provided Rs 50,000 to facilitate the operation, including expenses for purchasing a new phone, travel and hotel accommodation, as well as his subsequent exit.According to Joshi, Kabiruddin intended to carry out the terrorist act and then move to Pakistan."The accused intended to carry out this terrorist act and then migrate to Pakistan to join the ranks of Jaish-e-Mohammed, with the ultimate goal of attaining 'martyrdom'," he said.An FIR has been registered against the accused under the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act (UAPA) and various sections of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS). Proceedings are underway to produce Kabiruddin before the relevant court.
Article Summary: Mohammad Islam Kabiruddin, a native of Assam, had arrived in Vadodara after switching off his regular mobile phone and was staying at a hotel. Article Title: MNS leader threatens protest over Diljit Dosanjh concert, seeks ban on large events
Article Text:
(MNS has urged Mumbai Police to impose an immediate ban on live music concerts, large-scale entertainment events

NEW DELHI: The Maharashtra Navnirman Sena (MNS), led by Raj Thackeray, has urged Mumbai Police to impose an immediate ban on live music concerts and large-scale entertainment events at Mahalaxmi Racecourse and the NSCI Dome, alleging recurring incidents of drug consumption, traffic congestion and civic disruption.In a letter to the police, MNS leader Dinesh Dnyaneshwar Punde alleged that the two venues had become hubs for the sale and consumption of narcotics, particularly among young people. He cited a recent Anti-Narcotics Cell (ANC) crackdown and a previous fatal drug-related incident at a concert venue to press for a ban on such events.“Musical concerts are regularly held at Mahalaxmi Racecourse and NSCI Dome. During these events, drugs are openly sold and consumed, trapping the younger generation in the grip of addiction. At an event held on November 22, 2026, the ANC took action against 12-13 individuals for drug consumption. Even now, we have not forgotten the incident last year in which a young man lost his life at this very venue due to drug consumption. Furthermore, these concerts cause severe traffic congestion in the area, creating hardship for local residents,” the letter stated.Punde urged the police to stop granting permissions for concerts at both venues, warning that the party would join local residents in staging protests if the events were allowed to continue.“We have complete faith in the police administration; please do not let this trust be broken. We humbly request that permissions no longer be granted for musical concerts at Mahalaxmi Racecourse and NSCI Dome. If these concerts are not stopped, the MNS, along with local residents, will stage a Rasta Roko (road blockade) agitation at the location,” the letter read.The demand comes amid increased scrutiny of large-scale music events in Mumbai, including upcoming performances by singer Diljit Dosanjh. It also follows a November 22 police crackdown during which around 12-13 people were booked for alleged drug consumption at an event.Earlier this week, Mumbai Police deployed a newly launched ANC forensic van outside Mahalaxmi Racecourse as part of efforts to curb drug abuse at large gatherings.The mobile unit is equipped with five rapid detection machines and 360-degree surveillance cameras to help personnel identify narcotic substances and detect drug consumption.Explaining the equipment, Anti-Narcotics Cell Police Sub-Inspector Rohit Sali said the first machine, called 'TruNarc', uses Raman laser technology to identify substances without requiring the packaging to be opened.“The first machine is called ‘TruNarc,’ which contains a library of 1,325 narcotic drugs. It operates using a Raman laser effect. It can identify the drug inside a package without needing to open the polythene wrapping,” Sali said.The second machine, 'Gemini', has a wider database of substances, including narcotics, chemical precursors and explosives.“The second machine is ‘Gemini’, an advanced version of TruNarc. While TruNarc covers only narcotic drugs and their precursors, Gemini features a library of 15,000 substances, including narcotics, precursors, hazardous chemicals, and explosives,” he said.The third machine, the 'Dräger DrugTest 5000', is used to detect drug consumption through oral swab tests and can also analyse samples collected from surfaces.“The third machine is the ‘Dräger DrugTest 5000,’ which is designed for detecting drug consumption. It uses an oral swab; alternatively, if a substance is found on a surface, a sample can be collected and placed into a cassette, which then provides results within 10 minutes, identifying the substance,” Sali said.The MNS demand also comes against the backdrop of security concerns surrounding Dosanjh's event. Mumbai Police received a threatening email on Thursday warning of a blast at the mayor's office, grenade attacks at several locations across the city and improvised explosive devices (IEDs) at metro stations.The email also threatened violence linked to an event involving Dosanjh, prompting security checks on the anniversary of the 2008 Mumbai terror attacks. Police officials said the searches did not reveal anything suspicious.
Article Summary: The Maharashtra Navnirman Sena (MNS), led by Raj Thackeray, has urged Mumbai Police to impose an immediate ban on live music concerts. MNS leader Dinesh Dnyaneshwar Punde alleged that the two venues had become hubs for the sale and consumption of narcotics.

Article Title: Gujarat ATS arrests suspected Jaish-e-Mohammed terrorist in Vadodara, recovers rifle and ammunition
Article Text:
Gujarat ATS arrests suspected Jaish-linked terrorist

Hunt on for 65 Pakistani terrorists in Jammu and Kashmir

Security agencies intensify operations

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Terrorist numbers decline over the years

NEW DELHI: The Gujarat Anti-Terrorism Squad (ATS) has arrested a suspected Jaish-e-Mohammed (JeM) operative from Vadodara and recovered a rifle and more than 20 live cartridges from his possession, an ATS official said on Friday.The arrested accused has been identified as Md Saharul Islam, a resident of Assam, according to the official. A major operation by the ATS is currently underway, with further details awaited.The arrest comes amid heightened security operations against Pakistan-linked terror networks, particularly in Jammu and Kashmir, where security agencies are tracking an estimated 65 Pakistani terrorists operating across the Union Territory.According to officials in the security establishment, the presence of around 65 foreign terrorists has been confirmed through inputs from multiple intelligence agencies. Of these, 35 are believed to be affiliated with Lashkar-e-Taiba (LeT), 25 with Jaish-e-Mohammed, while the remaining operatives are linked to other banned terror outfits.The latest assessment comes days after the killing of Lateef Bhat, described by security officials as the last known active local terrorist in the Kashmir Valley.He was killed in an encounter with security forces in Jammu and Kashmir's Kulgam district on November 18, following an eight-day search operation.Officials said the estimated number of active terrorists in the Union Territory has declined from 91 in 2024, which included both foreign and local militants, to around 65 at present, comprising only Pakistani nationals.The security agencies are monitoring the presence of these foreign terrorists in districts including Poonch, Rajouri, Kishtwar and Doda, particularly in remote areas with dense forests and mountainous terrain. Officials said the figures are based on assessments by multiple agencies and may fluctuate as terrorists frequently change locations.The changing security landscape in Jammu and Kashmir follows a sustained decline in the number of active local militants. However, officials said Pakistan-origin terrorists continue to operate in parts of the Jammu region, making counter-infiltration operations and intelligence gathering a priority.Addressing the passing-out parade of probationary deputy superintendents of police, sub-inspectors and assistant directors of the Forest Protection Force at the Sher-i-Kashmir Police Academy in Udhampur on November 18, Lieutenant Governor Manoj Sinha expressed confidence that Jammu and Kashmir would soon become terror-free. He also asserted that only a handful of foreign terrorists remained in the Union Territory.Security agencies have been conducting multi-agency operations based on intelligence inputs to track and neutralise these operatives. Earlier this year, security forces neutralised all seven members of a Jaish-e-Mohammed group led by Saifullah in Kishtwar.The group had infiltrated in April 2024 and was eliminated through a series of operations culminating on February 22 in the Chatroo area under Operation Trashi-I.According to the available data, 135 terrorists were active in Jammu and Kashmir in 2022, including 85 foreign terrorists and 50 local militants. The number subsequently declined by nearly 48 in 2023, according to the figures provided.The reduction has been attributed to intensified counter-terrorism operations targeting active militants and their support networks.Despite the decline in local militant numbers, security agencies continue to focus on preventing cross-border infiltration, identifying logistical networks and tracking foreign terrorists operating in remote parts of the Union Territory.
Article Summary: Gujarat ATS arrests suspected Jaish-e-Mohammed (JeM) operative from Vadodara. Suspect identified as Md Saharul Islam, a resident of Assam. Arrest comes amid heightened security operations against Pakistan-linked terror networks. Security agencies are tracking an estimated 65 Pakistani terrorists in Jammu and Kashmir.

Article Title: 'Arrest me': CJP's Abhijit Dipke dares Mumbai Police, defies lookout circular at Nagpur rally
Article Text:
Representational Image. Cockroach Janata Party (CJP) founder Abhijeet Dipke

NEW DELHI: Cockroach Janata Party (CJP) founder and national convener Abhijeet Dipke on Thursday addressed a protest rally in Nagpur, challenging Mumbai Police to arrest him. The rally came even as Mumbai Police issued a Look Out Circular (LOC) against him in connection with an FIR linked to the party’s October 2 protest in Mumbai."There is a lookout notice against me by the Mumbai Police. There is police bandobast here and they are looking for me. Where is Abhijeet Dipke? I am here in Samvidhan Chowk. What will you do? Arrest me,” Dipke said, according to news agency ANI.“I have been in jail twice. Don't show me the fear of jail," he added, while addressing the CJP's 'Save Democracy, Save Constitution' rally at Samvidhan Chowk on Constitution Day.Mumbai Police issued LOCs against Dipke and CJP co-convenors Ashutosh Ranka and Saurav Das on Thursday. The circulars are linked to an FIR registered at Shivaji Park police station on October 3 over the party's protest held the previous day.The FIR names the organisers and between 400 and 500 unidentified attendees, invoking Sections 189 and 223 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), relating to unlawful assembly and disobedience to an order promulgated by a public servant.At the Nagpur rally, Dipke accused the BJP-led Centre of undermining the Constitution and alleged that institutions across the country had been hijacked."The government is acting against the Constitution. Not a single institution is left that has not been hijacked," he said.He also warned against what he described as the government's use of intimidation. "You have destroyed the country by intimidating people but this will not be tolerated. Show as much fear as you want for two more years. 2029 is approaching. This is India after Jantar Mantar," Dipke said.CJP co-convenor Ranka said the party would expand its activities beyond protests in major cities. "We will go to every village, interact with people and give a voice to the youth," he said.The LOCs come amid a separate legal challenge by Das, who was stopped from boarding a flight to the United Kingdom at Delhi's Indira Gandhi International Airport on November 23. He was scheduled to attend a panel discussion at Oxford.During proceedings before the Delhi High Court on Thursday, the Centre told Justice Amit Mahajan that the travel restriction had been initiated at the request of Maharashtra Police. Additional Solicitor General Chetan Sharma cited discrepancies in Das's educational background, address and parentage during record checks.Senior advocate Akhil Sibal, appearing for Das, argued that his client had not received prior notice or the underlying LOC order. "He has a valid passport and has a valid visa. He cannot be stopped from travelling as it is his fundamental right," Sibal told the court, according to ANI.
Article Summary: Cockroach Janata Party (CJP) founder and national convener Abhijeet Dipke challenged Mumbai Police to arrest him. Mumbai Police issued a Look Out Circular (LOC) against him in connection with an FIR linked to the party’s October 2 protest in Mumbai.

Article Title: 'We love Yogi very much': Sanjay Raut's praise puts spotlight on BJP's biggest UP question
Article Text:
Raut backs Yogi, calls him face of Hindutva

What Maurya said

Congress piles on

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Shiv Sena (UBT) MP Sanjay Raut on Thursday seemingly backed Uttar Pradesh chief minister Yogi Adityanath , describing him as the highest "face of Hindutva" and expressing confidence that he would continue to lead the state after the 2027 state assembly elections."If Yogi ji has declared himself (as CM face), it is commendable. He is a capable man, and we too love Yogi ji. Yogi ji is a face of Hindutva that stands at the very top, and if there is no Yogi, there is no UP. If Yogi ji has said this, then he has full confidence that his party will win a majority in Uttar Pradesh and that the majority of MLAs elected will support him," Raut said.Raut's "endorsement" has brought the question of the BJP's chief ministerial face in Uttar Pradesh into sharper focus, particularly after UP deputy CM Keshav Prasad Maurya asserted that a CM would be chosen by newly elected MLAs, rather than naming Adityanath as the party's automatic choice.While Adityanath's position as the BJP's most prominent leader in the state is undisputed, Maurya's remarks have revived speculation over whether the party will project the incumbent CM or leave the decision to its elected MLAs after the polls. The opposition seems to be now capitalising on the contrasting signals within the BJP.On Wednesday, Maurya had said the BJP's chief ministerial candidate would be decided by the party's elected MLAs after the Assembly elections, signalling that the party had not yet formally settled on a face for the next polls."BJP's face at the time of elections is the lotus flower, and elections are contested based on the lotus flower. After the elections, when MLAs are elected, their meeting is held, and central observers arrive," Maurya said, according to ANI.Asked whether he could be a contender for the post, Maurya said, "No individual decides this. SP, BSP, and Congress are private limited companies.""We have a system here. Whenever the leader of the legislative party is chosen, central observers come after the election. Whatever happens, you will find out in 2027," he added.Meanwhile, Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge on Thursday targeted the BJP over its performance in the 2024 Lok Sabha elections, crediting voters in Uttar Pradesh with checking the party's electoral ambitions and forcing Prime Minister Narendra Modi to abandon his '400 paar' slogan.Addressing a 'Samvidhan Raksha Sammelan' at the Congress office in Lucknow on Constitution Day, Kharge said the BJP had fallen well short of its target despite Modi repeatedly invoking the slogan during the election campaign."I thank the people of Uttar Pradesh. Prime Minister Narendra Modi used to say in all his speeches, wherever he went, 'Abki Baar, 400 Paar' (this time, more than 400 seats). But did the BJP cross 400 seats? The people sent you (BJP) packing. The people of Uttar Pradesh brought you to your knees. It is because of Uttar Pradesh that Modi is sitting quietly today," Kharge said.The BJP-led National Democratic Alliance (NDA) won 36 of Uttar Pradesh's 80 Lok Sabha seats in the 2024 general elections.Kharge also accused the BJP of allowing its funds to swell while people continued to grapple with inflation, unemployment and rising prices of cooking gas and essential food items. He further claimed that Union Home Minister Amit Shah had reduced his public statements, adding, "I do not know whether the two (Modi and Shah) are getting along or not."In an apparent reference to Adityanath, the Congress president also claimed that another leader in Lucknow had his eyes on the prime minister's chair.The political exchanges come as the Samajwadi Party (SP) and Congress continue discussions over a possible alliance for the 2027 Assembly elections. The SP has offered 26 seats to the Congress in the initial round of negotiations, while the Congress has sought 120 seats and is unwilling to settle for a lower number, according to sources.The SP is seeking to return to power after losing the 2017 and 2022 Assembly elections. It won 111 seats in the 2022 polls.
Article Summary: Shiv Sena (UBT) MP Sanjay Raut seemingly backs Uttar Pradesh chief minister Yogi Adityanath. Raut's "endorsement" has brought the question of the BJP's chief ministerial face in Uttar Pradesh into sharper focus. UP deputy CM Keshav Prasad Maurya asserted that a CM would be chosen by newly elected MLAs.

Article Title: Sheshnag Lake row: Karan Singh questions need for wider road, PDP steps up heat
Article Text:
Mehbooba demanded that the agreement be made public and asked why people were not being allowed to travel from Pahalgam to Chandanwari and beyond.

SRINAGAR: The controversy over the presence of heavy machinery near the ecologically fragile Sheshnag Lake along the Amarnath Yatra route shows no signs of dying down, with former Sadr-i-Riyasat (head of state) of Jammu & Kashmir, Karan Singh, saying every pilgrimage route need not be turned into a multi-lane road for the convenience of tourists. Mehbooba Mufti-led PDP has also stepped up its campaign, demanding that govt allow a joint team of politicians and environmentalists to visit the lake and make the site accessible for an independent assessment.Joining the voices opposing the move, Karan Singh, in a social media post, said: “We do not have to make every pilgrim route into a motorable road just for the convenience of tourists. Who authorised their movement, and what action has been taken against those responsible?” she asked at a press conference.Mehbooba said chief minister Omar Abdullah had signed a memorandum of understanding with the Border Roads Organisation (BRO) in Jan, assigning it the work of constructing a track in the area.She demanded that the agreement be made public and asked why people were not being allowed to travel from Pahalgam to Chandanwari and beyond.J&K government on Wednesday dismissed allegations of construction near the high-altitude lake, with Kaloo saying the JCB machinery was operating 200-300 feet away and at a higher elevation.As an online petition demanding an immediate halt to excavation and road-widening work near the lake crossed over 16,000 signatures Thursday, environmental activist Raja Muzaffar Bhat said he received a “distressing SOS” last night from a young nature lover, Zarqua Banday, who was allegedly being harassed for starting the petition. Article Title: Kashmir clerics split over Vande Mataram
Article Text:

SRINAGAR: A religious dispute over Vande Mataram at official functions in Kashmir escalated Thursday, with Sunni scholar Maulana Abdul Rashid Dawoodi challenging clerics to issue a fatwa on standing during its rendition and J&K’s grand mufti Nasir-ul-Islam declaring participation impermissible under Islamic law.Dawoodi urged scholars to settle whether standing for the national song as protocol amounted to polytheism or disbelief. “If any authentic organisation says that standing for Vande Mataram amounts to polytheism or disbelief, let it come forward with a fatwa,” he said.Dawoodi faced criticism after attending a J&K Waqf Board function in Srinagar on Monday, where all six stanzas of the song were played. He said standing as a matter of protocol should not automatically be equated with worship and accused critics of targeting him. “You cannot make statements recklessly,” he said, urging scholars to issue a fatwa on the specific question.The song was played under a Union home ministry protocol directive issued earlier this year mandating its full rendition at official functions, state events and legislature sessions.But grand mufti Nasir-ul-Islam, who heads the Muslim Personal Law Board, said attending a programme where Vande Mataram was sung or participating in its rendition was impermissible under Islamic law, citing sharia’s prohibition on worshipping created beings or bowing before them.Several clerics who attended Monday’s Waqf Day event, attended by Union minority affairs minister Kiren Rijiju, waqf board chairperson Darakhshan Andrabi and Lok Sabha MP Mian Altaf Ahmad, expressed regret on Wednesday and said they had prayed for repentance.

Article Title: 30 missing ultras working from Pakistan & PoK to revive terrorism in J&K: Police
Article Text:

JAMMU: Thirty terrorists from Reasi district who went missing between 1991 and 2003 had crossed over to Pakistan and Pakistan-occupied Kashmir to obtain arms and ammunition and training to “wage war against India” and disrupt peace in the Union territory, J&K Police announced late Wednesday.In an official release posted on X, police stated that these ultras — natives of Mahore and Chanana in Reasi — are now working for the Hizbul Mujahideen terror outfit in Pakistan, supplying arms, ammunition, and money in a bid to revive terrorism in J&K.
